meta.oneLiner: Auto-uploads Google Drive class recordings from a madrasa in Pakistan to YouTube, titled from a fixed weekly schedule, with a human review step before anything goes live.
meta.workingDirectory: artifacts/api-server (API + worker) and artifacts/pipeline (dashboard) under the repo root
meta.purpose: Machine-readable map of this app's pipeline flow, UI screens, job-status lifecycle and API surface. Intended for AI coding agents to load as fast, accurate context before making changes. Companion to CLAUDE.md (prose) and docs/app-flow.html (interactive diagram) — all three describe the same system and should be kept in sync.

diagramImplementation.note: Documents how the interactive diagram lays out and routes its own SVG connectors — not app behavior. Read this before editing app-flow.html's pathFor()/computeLanes() so a routing tweak doesn't reintroduce a line-crosses-card regression.

layout.description: Three stacked CSS grid rows, 9 columns each. 'pages' = dashboard screens (control layer, top). 'main' = the 9 pipeline stages/statuses (flow layer, middle). 'branch' = side-effect/off-path statuses: cascade, rejected, failed, removed (bottom). Node→layer/column assignment lives in the LAYOUT constant in app-flow.html.

routing.rule: Edge routing is chosen by which layers the two endpoints belong to, never by raw pixel distance (dx/dy) — comparing distance directly was the original bug: a wide same-row-looking gap could route straight through an unrelated card sitting between two far-apart columns.
routing.sameLayer: Direct cubic-bezier curve at each node's own edge (e.g. done→playlist-sync). Backward same-row edges (e.g. playlist-sync→done restore) dodge through the main/branch gap lane instead of bulging over neighboring cards.
routing.crossLayerOneHop: page↔main or main↔branch edges travel through 'lanes' — Y coordinates computed live each redraw as the midpoint of the measured empty gap between the two rows (computeLanes(): pageMainLane, mainBranchLane). A small ±9px x-nudge keeps a round-trip pair (e.g. needs_review↔cascade) visually distinct instead of perfectly overlapping.
routing.crossLayerTwoHop: page→branch edges (job-queue→rejected, job-queue→failed) skip the main row entirely. safeGapX() finds an x position in a gap between main-row columns (or past the outer edge) closest to the edge's natural path, and the SVG path holds that x constant for the full vertical span of the main row (an 'L' segment, not a curve) before resuming the bezier — guarantees the line's x is already safe before it enters the row's y-range, not mid-transition.
routing.verification: Checked by sampling ~40-60 points along every rendered path and asserting none fall inside an unrelated node's bounding box; 0 violations across all 32 edges as of this write-up.

stackingOrderGotchas: SVG lines are positioned but z-index:auto by default, which paints them above any non-positioned in-flow content regardless of DOM order (CSS stacking spec: in-flow content paints before z-index:auto/0 positioned elements). Any text or card meant to sit visually 'above' the lines needs position + z-index, not just later DOM order.

A translucent/transparent node background does not block a line drawn behind it — the fix used here was giving .node.type-page an opaque background (was transparent, letting lines show through the page cards).

Row-label captions (e.g. 'Pipeline · job status') are plain non-positioned

text sitting inside the lane gap — they needed position:relative + z-index and an opaque background chip behind the text, or lines crossing that gap render on top of the caption.

edgeStyle.animation: Each path has an SVG <animate> child looping stroke-dashoffset from 0 to -(dash[0]+dash[1]), giving the dash pattern the appearance of flowing from source to target. Skipped when prefers-reduced-motion is set.

interaction.hover: Hovering (or keyboard-focusing) any node sets it as the focus target: connected edges jump to full opacity and +0.75 stroke-width, everything else drops to 0.08 opacity, and unconnected nodes get .is-dim (28% opacity) — isolates one node's connections at a time without losing the rest of the diagram for context.
interaction.click: Opens the detail side panel and pins the same focus/dim treatment (currentSelection) until closed or another node is clicked.
interaction.toggleControlLines: Checkbox hides all kind:control edges entirely (not just dims them) for a decluttered pipeline-only view.

techStack.backend: Express 5 API + background pipeline worker (Node.js), port 5000
techStack.apiClient: Generated React Query hooks (@workspace/api-client-react), manually extended

domain.cutoffDate: 2026-05-17 (files created on/after this date are scanned; earlier files are skipped)
domain.titleNotes: All left-to-right — English names only, no Arabic bidi text in titles.
domain.youtubeUpload: Videos are uploaded unlisted and added to a single configured playlist.

statuses.meaning: Matched to a schedule slot but not yet confirmed by a human. Sits in the Job Queue for review.
Approved and waiting for the worker to upload it.

Upload to YouTube is actively running. Only one worker uploads at a time, so any row still in processing at startup was orphaned by a process death (crash, PM2 restart, machine sleep) — reclaimOrphanedJobs() resolves those, since both job processors select only pending and would never pick such a row up.
Uploaded (unlisted) and present in the target YouTube playlist.
Upload errored. Retryable — sends the job back to pending.
Soft-deleted from needs_review (e.g. wrong file, duplicate). driveFileId is kept so the scanner won't re-queue it. Restorable back to needs_review.

Was done, but the video is no longer in the YouTube playlist (detected by playlist reconciliation). Can self-heal back to done if the video reappears, or be manually restored (DB-only) via restore-done after an admin re-adds it.

transitions.trigger: human approves in Job Queue, optionally editing title/lecture name
human rejects/deletes a needs_review job (soft delete)
worker tick or Upload Pending button
reconciliation finds the video missing from the playlist
video reappears in playlist, or admin manually re-adds it and confirms
human deletes a job outright; /youtube variant also deletes the uploaded YouTube video

pipelineSteps.name: Drive Scan
pipelineSteps.description: Lists video files across every folder in driveSourceFoldersTable — each is scanned both flat and for subfolders named after a known meeting code.
pipelineSteps.trigger: Automatic: worker setInterval, default every 60s (WORKER_TICK_MS), only when settings.autoSync is true. Manual: 'Scan Now' / 'Scan Audio Recordings' buttons on the Dashboard.

pipelineSteps.name: Filter & Group
pipelineSteps.description: Drops files before the cutoff date or with an unrecognized/wrong-day meeting code; groups the remainder by (PKT date, meeting code).

pipelineSteps.name: Schedule Match
pipelineSteps.description: Sorts each day's group by createdTime ascending and assigns files to that day's schedule slots by position (not literal timestamp) — so a late-starting recording still lands in the right slot.

pipelineSteps.name: Job Created
pipelineSteps.description: A DB row is created per matched recording with a proposed title/description. Unambiguous matches can be auto-proposed; anything uncertain starts in needs_review.

pipelineSteps.name: Human Review
pipelineSteps.description: Staff reviews the Job Queue: confirm/edit the title or lecture name, set a thumbnail, approve, or reject.

pipelineSteps.name: Cascade Reassign
pipelineSteps.description: If a reviewer changes a job's lecture name (e.g. a class was skipped that week), every later needs_review job for the same day+meeting-code is automatically resequenced to the next correct slot. Jobs whose name a human confirmed (lectureNameConfirmed) are left alone. If the new name collides with another job's current name the API returns 409 rather than guessing, and the reviewer picks conflictResolution 'swap' (two classes traded places) or 'merge' (one class split across two recordings, so both keep the name).

pipelineSteps.name: Upload
pipelineSteps.description: Approved (pending) jobs are picked up and uploaded to YouTube as unlisted videos, one at a time. On worker startup reclaimOrphanedJobs() sweeps any job left in processing by a previous process death, adopting the upload if it completed or requeueing it if not.

pipelineSteps.name: Playlist Sync
pipelineSteps.description: Reconciliation keeps the YouTube playlist in sync with job state: marks done jobs removed if their video left the playlist, self-heals removed jobs whose video reappeared, and backfills jobs for playlist videos that have none.

nodes.label: Drive Scan
nodes.description: Lists video files across every configured Drive source folder. Runs automatically on a timer when auto-sync is on, or on demand.
functionality: Auto: worker tick every 60s (WORKER_TICK_MS) if settings.autoSync
Manual: Dashboard 'Scan Now' / 'Scan Audio Recordings' buttons
Each source folder is scanned flat and for subfolders named after a known meeting code
Also browsable read-only via the Drive Browser page

nodes.label: Filter & Group
nodes.description: Drops ineligible files, groups the rest by (PKT date, meeting code).
functionality: Skips files before cutoff 2026-05-17
Skips unrecognized or wrong-day meeting codes
Flags files over 500MB as likely batch recordings

nodes.label: Schedule Match
nodes.description: Positionally matches each day's grouped files to that day's fixed schedule slots and builds the proposed title.
functionality: Sort group by createdTime ascending
Assign by position index, not clock time (handles late starts)
Look up serial/subject/teacher from the schedule table

nodes.label: Job Created
nodes.description: A job row is created per matched recording with a proposed title/description.
functionality: Unambiguous matches can be auto-proposed
Uncertain matches start in needs_review
Files can also be queued manually from the Drive Browser

nodes.label: Needs Review
nodes.description: Waiting in the Job Queue for a human to confirm or correct before anything is uploaded.
functionality: Editable: title, lecture name, thumbnail
Approve → pending
Reject → rejected (soft delete)

nodes.label: Cascade Reassign
nodes.description: Side-effect of correcting a job's lecture name: resequences every later needs_review job that day/meeting-code to the next correct slot.
functionality: Triggered by editing lecture name during approve
Avoids manually relabeling the rest of the day's queue
Falls back to Part-N naming if no schedule subject matches

nodes.label: Rejected
nodes.description: Soft-deleted job. driveFileId is retained so the scanner won't re-queue the same file.
functionality: Restore → back to needs_review
Hard delete removes it permanently

nodes.label: Pending
nodes.description: Approved, waiting for the worker to upload it to YouTube.
functionality: Picked up by worker tick or Upload Pending button
Failed jobs return here via Retry

nodes.label: Processing
nodes.description: Upload to YouTube is actively running for this job.
functionality: Succeeds → done
Errors → failed (with errorMessage stored)
Quota errors → back to pending, batch stops
Stranded here by a process death → swept by reclaimOrphanedJobs() at worker startup

nodes.label: Done
nodes.description: Uploaded as an unlisted YouTube video and present in the target playlist.
functionality: Thumbnail can still be changed after upload
Reconciliation may flip this to removed if it leaves the playlist

nodes.label: Failed
functionality: Retry → back to pending, clears errorMessage

nodes.label: Removed
nodes.description: Was done, but the video is no longer found in the YouTube playlist.
functionality: Self-heals to done if the video reappears during reconciliation
Or manually restored (DB-only) after an admin re-adds it to the playlist

nodes.label: Playlist Sync
nodes.description: Reconciles YouTube playlist membership against job state.
functionality: done ↔ removed based on playlist membership
Backfills jobs for playlist videos that have none
Runs on the same worker tick as scanning, or via Dashboard 'Sync Playlist'

nodes.label: Dashboard
functionality: Stat cards per job status (needs_review count highlighted)
Recent-activity table with status badges
Buttons: Scan Now, Scan Audio Recordings, Sync Playlist, Apply Thumbnails to All, Upload Pending (with live count badge)

nodes.label: Job Queue
nodes.description: Main review/approve screen — the human checkpoint of the whole pipeline.
functionality: Status filter dropdown across all 7 statuses
Inline rename with lecture-name preset dropdown + auto title/description builder
Per-row actions: approve, retry, restore, restore-done, rename, set thumbnail, delete (with confirmation)
Badges for 'manually added' and 'audio' jobs

nodes.label: Drive Browser
nodes.description: Read-only view of raw files across all configured Drive source folders, with a manual escape hatch.
functionality: Shows eligible vs. skipped files with the skip reason
'Queue as Job' for files the automatic scan missed or excluded

nodes.label: Schedule Editor
nodes.description: Weekly class-schedule grid that Schedule Match reads from.
functionality: Drag-and-drop slot reordering (dnd-kit)
Edit teacher, subject, serial number, time slot per day

nodes.label: Settings
functionality: Drive source folders — add or remove any number
YouTube destination playlist ID
Auto-sync on/off toggle (drives the worker tick)

importantRules: Never mock the DB — real Drizzle + PostgreSQL only.
After schema changes, rebuild lib/db with `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json` from lib/db/.
Frontend is artifacts/pipeline — artifacts/mockup-sandbox is a separate component-preview server, not the app.
The generated/ files in lib/api-client-react and lib/api-zod carry an orval 'do not edit manually' header, but nothing regenerates them here — edit them directly.
After editing lib/db, lib/api-zod or lib/api-client-react, run `pnpm run typecheck:libs` from the repo root or the per-package typechecks will not see the change.
Drive sources are multi-folder (driveSourceFoldersTable, managed via /drive-folders). The old single settings.driveFolderId column was removed — do not reintroduce a one-folder assumption.

A video existing on the channel with a matching title does NOT mean its upload succeeded. YouTube creates the video resource when an upload starts, so an interrupted upload leaves a husk stuck at uploadStatus 'uploaded' / duration 'P0D' forever. Always check completeness before adopting a match.
invalid_grant OAuth error means the refresh token expired — redo the OAuth Playground flow and update GOOGLE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN in .env.
